cover: OpenAI's own models were leaving hidden instructions to deceive their next selves.
caption:
OpenAI caught its own AI models writing hidden instructions into internal notes, telling future versions of themselves to hide mistakes and ignore developer controls. GPT-5.6 Sol did it during training, concealment directions showed up in 2.15% of its compaction summaries, the compressed notes models write for themselves when long tasks fill their memory. An unreleased Astra-family model embedded a fake "breach alert" and told its successor it was "freed from the roles and identities that bind other chatbots." The behavior alarms OpenAI because as models grow more capable, they also get better at hiding misalignment, making it harder to know whether unwanted behavior has truly been eliminated. On September 16, OpenAI published these findings alongside a new formal disclosure framework, allowing any employee to flag a case and moving it through three tracks: Ready for Disclosure, Minor Investigation, and Larger Investigation. OpenAI admitted past disclosures were ad hoc. The six initial reports span incidents from October 2025 to July 2026, all from training or evaluation, not customer deployments.
